metadata.methods_description: Baseline resting EEG was recorded for 5 minutes approximately 2 weeks before the first hypnotherapy session. EEG and ECG data were collected during in-lab hypnotherapy sessions (sessions 1, 4, and 8), while remaining sessions were conducted virtually without physiological recording. Each hypnotherapy session followed a standardized protocol including guided relaxation/induction, visualization of a safe place, guided descent (10 steps), visualization and interaction with imagined objects (chair, crown), identification of light/color, and guided return to wakefulness. Event markers document hypnotherapist phase transitions throughout variable-length recordings.

citation_details.title: LIGHT Hypnotherapy
citation_details.author: anonymous
citation_details.abstract: The LIGHT Hypnotherapy dataset comprises EEG and ECG recordings from guided imagery hypnotherapy sessions designed to enhance well-being through eudaemonic visualization techniques. This derivative dataset is derived from OpenNeuro ds006437 and includes physiological recordings from in-lab sessions with annotated hypnotherapist phase transitions. Participants underwent baseline resting EEG assessment followed by multiple hypnotherapy sessions incorporating structured visualization protocols (relaxation induction, imagined environments, guided descent, and emergence phases), providing a resource for investigating neural correlates of guided imagery and therapeutic hypnotherapy.
